In their efforts to oppose commonsense reforms to strengthen Medicaid and ensure its sustainability for the most vulnerable and future Americans, Democrats are once again resorting to fear mongering—not facts.

Below is a breakdown of common Democratic myths and the real facts about the Big Beautiful Bill (BBB) Medicaid provisions:

⸻

DEMOCRAT FEAR MONGERING:

Millions will lose access to Medicaid under cruel new work requirements.

FACT:
The BBB’s Medicaid community engagement provisions apply only to able-bodied adults without dependents—not to seniors, people with disabilities, pregnant women, or caregivers.
Beginning January 1, 2026, these adults can meet the requirement by working, volunteering, attending school, or participating in job training for at least 80 hours a month.

This is not punitive—it’s empowering. It recognizes that Medicaid should support not just health but upward mobility and personal responsibility.

⸻

DEMOCRAT FEAR MONGERING:

Medicaid recipients will be kicked off the program due to paperwork errors and red tape.

FACT:
The BBB combats fraud, waste, and abuse, not eligible recipients.
For example, it ends the “good faith” waiver by 2030, ensuring states can no longer dodge accountability for improper payments to ineligible individuals or providers.

It uses the SSA Death Master File to prevent payments to deceased individuals and creates a federal system to prevent dual-state enrollment.

Verifying eligibility is not “red tape”—it’s responsible governance.

⸻

DEMOCRAT FEAR MONGERING:

The bill targets immigrants and punishes those in need.

FACT:
Federal law has long required that Medicaid recipients be citizens or legal residents.

The BBB strengthens enforcement by ending federal funding during the 90-day verification period for those without verified status.

No funding will go to those who are ineligible under federal law—this includes approximately 1.4 million illegal immigrants and 1.2 million other ineligible individuals who are currently on the rolls. 

⸻

DEMOCRAT FEAR MONGERING:

States will be penalized for trying to provide compassionate care.

FACT:
Beginning in 2028, states that deliberately fund health care for undocumented immigrants through Medicaid-like programs will face a 10% reduction in federal Medicaid matching funds.

This ensures that Medicaid remains focused on U.S. citizens and legal residents—the populations it was designed to serve.

⸻

DEMOCRAT FEAR MONGERING:

These changes are meant to slash Medicaid and gut funding.

FACT:
The BBB doesn’t slash Medicaid—it strengthens it.

By removing ineligible individuals and focusing resources on those truly in need, the reforms ensure long-term sustainability of the program.

Medicaid spending is projected to grow under the BBB, not shrink, because the focus is on integrity and efficiency—not cuts.

⸻

Bottom Line:
The BBB reforms don’t weaken Medicaid—they preserve it for those who need it most: vulnerable seniors, low-income children, people with disabilities, and legal working families.

Democrats are trying to protect bureaucracy. Republicans are fighting to protect people.

This morning on @Varneyco, I discussed Democrats' fear-mongering on common sense Medicaid reform.  

The Big Beautiful Bill saves money for American families while strengthening Medicaid for our most vulnerable—seniors, children, people with disabilities, and legal residents—by ensuring no funds go to ineligible recipients.  

President Trump's plan to lower perscription drug costs could also save an additional $1 trillion over the next decade.  

The BBB provides a solid framework, but we must continue to build on this important first step.

Don’t miss today’s @ReportVolpe on @FOX56WOLF at 10:30am.

I sat down with House Majority Leader @SteveScalise and @RepBresnahan to discuss the BBB and clear up the misleading claims being made about Medicaid. 

Important conversation—you’ll want to see it. https://t.co/Um1TdKEdtR

Had a substantive and timely conversation on @ReportVolpe with House Majority Leader @SteveScalise  and  @RepBresnahan. 

We laid out the truth about the BBB—cutting through the fear mongering about Medicaid and explaining how this legislation supports working families, empowers small businesses, grows the economy, fortifies our border security, and unleashes American energy dominance.

Check out the full interview below!

Despite the media’s falsehoods and Democrat fearmongering, eligible American citizens will not lose Medicaid coverage under the One Big Beautiful Bill.
 
This legislation strengthens Medicaid for those who are eligible under the law by rooting out waste, fraud, and abuse—not by targeting the vulnerable. In fact, Medicaid spending has increased 57% over the last five years, underscoring the urgent need for responsible reforms that protect the program’s future.
 
Here are the facts, the only individuals affected by these reforms are those who do not meet eligibility or participation standards:
 
▪️ Able-bodied adults without dependents who choose not to meet modest 20-hour-per-week work, education, or service requirements

▪️ Illegal immigrants who were never eligible in the first place

▪️ Ineligible individuals improperly kept on the rolls under Biden-era policies
 
Republicans are restoring integrity to the program and protecting Medicaid for seniors, the disabled, and low-income families who rely on it.
 
Learn more below: https://t.co/zw4057KV37

The House’s version of the OBBB rightly sought to remove all illegal immigrants—roughly 1.4 million—from Medicaid rolls. While the Senate ruled that provision out under the Byrd Rule, the final compromise still ensures Medicaid’s integrity and protects resources for American citizens:

•Illegal immigrants are no longer eligible for Medicaid, except in very limited emergency situations—which account for less than 4% of all claims. Under federal law, emergency medical care will still be provided to all who need treatment.

•Starting Oct. 1, 2026, states with illegal immigrants enrolled in their Medicaid program will see their federal reimbursement reduced, shifting more of the cost to states that choose to ignore federal law.

•Only U.S. citizens, nationals, or lawful residents will qualify for full Medicaid reimbursement—the other 96% of claims.

This isn’t about denying care—it’s about ensuring that care goes to those who are here legally and preserving the long-term integrity of Medicaid. If blue states want to continue subsidizing illegal immigration, they’ll have to do it without relying on federal taxpayers.

The @HouseGOP is on the verge of delivering major wins for the American people.

The One Big Beautiful Bill prevents a massive tax hike on working families and small businesses, grows our economy, strengthens border security, promotes American energy dominance, and makes Medicaid more sustainable—protecting care for those it was meant to serve: seniors, the disabled, and low-income families.

The American people sent us to Washington to deliver results—and that’s exactly what we’re doing. We’re working with President @realDonaldTrump to advance the America First Agenda and make our country as great as it can be.

This morning on @Varneyco, I explained how the One Big Beautiful Bill ensures that federal Medicaid dollars go where they’re supposed to—to eligible American citizens the program was intended to support.

Under this legislation, states can no longer expect federal taxpayers to foot the bill for illegal immigrants on Medicaid. If they choose to cover those costs, they’ll have to do so without federal support.

Despite the rhetoric, no one who is eligible for Medicaid will lose coverage—period. The OBBB protects the long-term integrity of the program and ensures it serves seniors, low-income families, and the disabled.

And to strengthen care in underserved communities, we’re also investing $50 billion to support rural hospitals and ensure continued access to care across the country.

House Republicans are bringing accountability back—rooting out waste, fraud, and abuse and restoring confidence government programs.

Yesterday, I met with members of the National Coalition for Assistive and Rehab Technology (NCART) to discuss the importance of ensuring access to Complex Rehab Technology (CRT) for individuals with disabilities.

We spoke about the need for Medicare coverage of power standing systems, removing obstacles for beneficiaries to obtain a titanium or carbon fiber wheelchair, and maintaining access to telehealth services in rural communities.

Today on @CNN News Central, I discussed the looming budget deadline and why Democrats’ demands are unreasonable. They’re pushing for hundreds of billions in new spending, stripping out commonsense Medicaid work requirements, and making ACA subsidies for wealthy individuals permanent—all while rejecting future cost-saving measures. That’s not responsible governing. We can work together to improve the ACA, but reforms should come after we secure a responsible budget agreement, not as leverage for a shutdown.

I also weighed in on the potential indictment of former FBI Director James Comey. For years, Comey pursued President Trump on the false Steele dossier—something he knew was fueled by political motivation and not credible.

That abuse of power eroded trust in the FBI. If prosecutors believe there is credible evidence, they must follow the law and the Constitution wherever it leads. Restoring the credibility of our institutions is critical for our country.

This week, President Trump announced a major agreement with Pfizer which is an important first step to lowering the cost of prescription for Americans. Pfizer will be offering lower costs for prescription drugs to Medicare as well as offering major pharmaceuticals at a steep discount directly to consumers through TrumpRx.

In addition to offering prescription at lower costs to consumers, Pfizer committed $70 billion towards on-shoring manufacturing.

I’ve been a strong advocate of lowering prescription drug prices for both public and private payers. It never made sense that the largest purchaser of prescription drugs could not negotiate with pharmaceutical companies to pass on savings to consumers. President Trump and his administration saw it the same way.

I want to thank President Trump, @SecKennedy, @DrOzCMS, and Director of Medicare and Deputy Administrator of CMS Klomp for their work towards achieving this great outcome for Americans.

President Trump has no particular special interest in influencing. President Trump‘s only special interest is the best for the American people and achieving real results, lowering the costs of healthcare for all.

Earlier today, I joined The Bob Cordaro Show to set the record straight on the Democrats’ shutdown games.

Democrats are not being truthful about this shutdown. They are holding government funding hostage over giving Medicaid to illegal immigrants and adding $1.4 trillion in new spending.

Republicans voted to keep the government open with a clean, short-term funding bill that Chuck Schumer and Democrats continue to block.

This shutdown is senseless. It helps no one. It is hurting families, small businesses, and programs like WIC that many Pennsylvanians rely on. Enough is enough. It’s time for Democrats to stop the obstruction and work with us to responsibly fund government.

Today, @POTUS  announced a major agreement with @AstraZeneca, who will now lower prescription drug costs for Medicare and other major pharmaceuticals at a steep discount directly to consumers through TrumpRx. In addition to offering prescription drugs at lower costs to consumers, @AstraZenecaUS committed $50 billion towards on-shoring manufacturing, and research and development.

This follows his recent announcement of a similar agreement with @pfizer, further expanding access to affordable prescription drugs for all Americans. I’ve been a strong advocate of lowering prescription drug prices for both public and private payers and will work to ensure more pharmaceutical companies negotiate with the Trump Administration and pass on savings to consumers. 

I highly commend President Trump for his leadership on this extremely important issue and I will continue to work with him both to reduce our country's deficit spending and to lower costs to working families and all Americans.

Because of Democrats’ irrational demands for healthcare for illegal immigrants, gutting the BBB, and spending another $1.4 trillion of taxpayer money, our government remains shut down after 17 days. They’ve now voted ten times against keeping the government open and our federal workers paid, showing exactly where their priorities lie.

Instead of working to reopen the government, Democrats are doubling down on their anti-American agenda with events like the “No Kings” protests planned for Saturday.

But while the left tries to hold us back and stall progress, President Trump continues moving forward, and so will we.

This is an important discussion and is clearly a debate within the banking community. We must ensure deposits are protected, expand access to capital, make lending cheaper, increase affordability for small businesses, and Make Community Banking Great Again.

This month, @HouseGOP passed the Lower Health Care Premiums for All Americans Act which address rising healthcare costs, including premiums that have rose over 60% since the passage of the Affordable Care Act. 

We can lower the cost of healthcare, only if Democrats decide to put people over politics.

Republicans will continue to support policies that deliver affordable care and lower premiums for all Americans.
